statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is in the low band on observed two-sided overnight structure; a narrow elevated window is flagged around the U.S. cash open and the flash PMI release.
recommendation: Conditions are consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour outside a narrow checkpoint window of 13:30-14:30 UTC (15:30-16:30 Berlin), when the opening auction and the S&P Global flash PMIs coincide. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a narrow two-sided overnight range at record levels; low Tail with a flagged open plus flash-PMI checkpoint
body: NQ futures are trading near 31,033, roughly flat against the prior settle and mid-range inside an overnight band of approximately 30,983-31,095 (about 0.36%). That band contains the contract's 52-week high, so the index is at record territory, but the observed structure is two-sided rotation rather than persistent one-way extension: there is no repeated extension after failed retracements and no holding at a session extreme. VIX near 14.2 confirms a calm volatility backdrop. The Nasdaq Composite closed at a record 27,244.28 on 22 September, its second consecutive record, led by semiconductors on a sixth straight advancing session, so the multi-day regime is a bullish uptrend even though the current hour is range-bound. Cross-asset evidence is mixed rather than aligned: Treasury yields are elevated, with the 10Y near 4.96% and the 2Y near 4.76% following the FOMC's 25bp hike to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September and a dot plot signalling further tightening, which trims long-duration tech at the margin. Crude has fallen for a sixth consecutive session, with WTI near $89.54 and Brent near $98.90, after Saudi Aramco restarted the East-West pipeline and U.S.-Iran talks showed reported progress. That combination is a de-escalation impulse on the dominant geopolitical file and reduces the discontinuity channel that has driven this year's tail episodes. Tail is therefore held at 12: the aligned bullish regime is a conditional amplifier for the U.S. open, not observed pathological structure. Stress at 36 reflects the elevated rate path, structurally high oil and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz situation. The flagged window covers the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 13:45 UTC S&P Global flash PMIs, the session's only scheduled macro checkpoint; conditional Tail peaks at 20 in the 14:00 UTC hour and decays thereafter on the base case of orderly price discovery. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was partial and about three and a half hours old at assessment time, so it was treated as stale and excluded; this assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment. Tail moved between 10 and 21 with three WATCH hours around the 22 September U.S. cash open (14:00 UTC) and the 18:00-19:00 UTC afternoon, each resolving back to the low band within one to two hours. The overnight cycle from 02:00 UTC onward settled into a normal, range-bound mode with Tail between 10 and 12 and Stress easing from 37 to 33 before firming modestly to 36 into the European morning. Confidence held between 84 and 88 throughout, indicating continuous usable evidence with no gap in coverage.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the low band for most of the 24-hour horizon and concentrates conditional risk in a single narrow window. Tail rises from 12 to 18 in the 13:00 UTC hour and peaks at 20 in the 14:00 UTC hour, the one WATCH slot, where the opening auction and the flash PMIs coincide with the index at record levels; a 52-week futures high overnight makes opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks the specific conditional amplifier to test. On the base case of orderly price discovery, Tail decays to 17 by 15:00 UTC and 14 by 17:00 UTC, with a secondary rise to 17 in the 19:00 UTC power hour on closing-auction imbalance. The overnight cycle returns to 10-11 with no scheduled U.S. macro release, then firms to 12 into the European morning as Thursday's 12:30 UTC jobless claims approach. Confidence declines gradually from 87 to 85 across the horizon as evidence distance from the assessment cutoff grows.
